question.problem:
Given that $J(t)={\int }_{0}^{1}(3x-\operatorname{cos}⁡(t))^{2}\,\text{d}x,$ calculate ${J}^{′}(t)$ for $t\in R$ by differentiating under the integral sign.

${J}^{′}(t)=\operatorname{sin}⁡t(\,$
{{field-1}}$)$
question.worked_solution:
Suppose $f(x,t)$ is continuous on $R=[a,b]\times [c,d]$ and $\frac{∂f}{∂t}$ exists and is continuous on $R.$ Then, the function

$$
F(t)={\int }_{a}^{b}f(x,t)\,\text{d}x
$$

is differentiable on $(c,d),$ and

$$
{F}^{′}(t)=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x,t)\,\text{d}x={\int }_{a}^{b}\frac{∂f}{∂t}(x,t)\,\text{d}x.
$$

This is known as differentiating under the integral sign.

We wish to compute ${J}^{′}(t),$ where

$$
J(t)={\int }_{0}^{1}(3x-\operatorname{cos}⁡(t))^{2}\,\text{d}x.
$$

Differentiating under the integral sign, we get

$$
{J}^{′}(t)={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{∂}{∂t}[(3x-\operatorname{cos}⁡(t))^{2}]\,\text{d}x.
$$

Next, let's compute the partial derivative with respect to $t$:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂t}[(3x-\operatorname{cos}⁡(t))^{2}] & =2(3x-\operatorname{cos}⁡(t))\cdot \frac{∂}{∂t}(3x-\operatorname{cos}⁡(t)) \\  & =2(3x-\operatorname{cos}⁡(t))\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(t) \\  & =2\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)(3x-\operatorname{cos}⁡(t))\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting this back into our integral, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{J}^{′}(t) & ={\int }_{0}^{1}2\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)(3x-\operatorname{cos}⁡(t))\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\operatorname{sin}⁡(t){\int }_{0}^{1}(3x-\operatorname{cos}⁡(t))\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, let's evaluate the remaining integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}(3x-\operatorname{cos}⁡(t))\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{1}3x\,\text{d}x-{\int }_{0}^{1}\operatorname{cos}⁡(t)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3{x}^{2}}{2}{|}_{0}^{1}-\operatorname{cos}⁡(t)\cdot x{|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{3}{2}-\operatorname{cos}⁡(t)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{J}^{′}(t) & =2\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)(\frac{3}{2}-\operatorname{cos}⁡(t)) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)(3-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(t)).\end{aligned}
$$
